papers.title: Nucleus accumbens acetylcholine dips track reward value and temporal costs to shape delay discounting
papers.abstract: As an organism chooses between competing rewards, it must often integrate learned reward value with the changing costs associated with obtaining them. Yet, the brain mechanisms through which these factors jointly guide choice are not well understood. Previous studies have shown that dopamine signals in the nucleus accumbens (NAc) track reward value and are modulated by their associated delay costs. Our prior work further implicated NAc cholinergic interneurons by demonstrating that dopamine D2 receptors in these neurons influence choice under temporal, but not probabilistic, costs. However, whether NAc acetylcholine (ACh) dynamics track reward value and/or delay, and whether they contribute to adaptive choice, remains unknown. Using in vivo fiber photometry during a delay discounting task in which mice choose between a small, immediate reward and a larger, delayed reward, we reveal that cue-evoked ACh dips dynamically track relative reward magnitude and are diminished by increasing delays. Our data further show that optogenetically enhancing these dips attenuates the delay-dependent decline in choice of the larger, delayed reward. These findings identify a previously unrecognized role for NAc cue-evoked ACh dips in shaping adaptive choice as temporal costs increase.

papers.title: LAMA2-related muscular dystrophy alters Schwann cell calcium homeostasis and increases peripheral nerve inflammation
papers.abstract: LAMA2-related muscular dystrophy (LAMA2-RD) affects skeletal muscle and peripheral nerves, yet the consequences of LAMA2 deficiency on peripheral nerve integrity beyond early postnatal development remain incompletely understood. We investigated sciatic nerve architecture and molecular alterations across postnatal life in hypomorphic Lama2dy2J/dy2J mice. LAMA2 localizes around the abaxonal surface of myelinating Schwann cells in control nerves. LAMA2-deficient nerves exhibited patchy regions lacking myelinated axons from early postnatal stages into adulthood, including expanded Remak bundles along with axons completely lacking normal Schwann cell ensheathment. In adult nerves, myelin infolding and reduced myelin circularity revealed abnormalities in the architecture of myelin that had formed. Bulk sciatic nerve RNA sequencing identified altered calcium-signaling and immune-related transcriptional signatures. Complementary Fura Red measurements in primary nerve-derived Schwann cell cultures demonstrated decreased intracellular calcium in LAMA2-deficient samples, while ATP-evoked responses were preserved. Older LAMA2-deficient nerves also exhibited increased CD45+CD11b+ myeloid-cell infiltration. Together, these observations extend the characterization of LAMA2-associated neuropathy into adulthood and identify calcium homeostasis and neuroimmune responses as candidate processes relevant to persistent peripheral nerve pathology.

papers.title: Mapping Endogenous Psychedelic Chemistry: Indolethylamine N-Methyltransferase (INMT) Localizes Proximal to the Golgi Apparatus of Human Neurons
papers.abstract: N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT) is a serotonergic psychedelic with a history of ethnobotanical use and emerging clinical efficacy for neuropsychiatric disorders. Following Julius Axelrod's pioneering studies showing DMT production in human tissues, DMT has been proposed as an endogenous neuromodulator because it is a serotonin 2A receptor (5-HT2A R) agonist. However, the DMT-producing enzyme, indolethylamine N-methyltransferase (INMT), has not been characterized at the protein level in the human central nervous system. Here, we validated an anti-INMT antibody and used immunocytochemistry to show that INMT localizes in close proximity to other DMT biosynthetic enzymes near the cytosolic face of the cis-Golgi network in human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons, with immunoreactivity observed across multiple neuronal Golgi phenotypes. Notably, both DMT-like and 5-HT2A R immunoreactivity also partially localized in close proximity to the Golgi apparatus. Our results establish the first protein-level characterization of INMT in human neurons and identify the cis-Golgi network as a candidate microdomain for psychedelic tryptamine biosynthesis. We propose that INMT catalytic activity at the cis-Golgi network creates an enriched region of membrane-permeable psychedelic tryptamines that can access an intracellular 5- HT2A R pool. These findings provide new tools and insights that can inform efforts to understand the mechanism of action of psychedelics under clinical investigation and to target endogenous tryptamines therapeutically.

papers.title: Endothelin-1 from Tongue Glands Gates 1 Sodium Taste and Intake
papers.abstract: Sodium is an essential nutrient. To survive sodium deficiency, animals dramatically increase their appetite for salt. However, whether and how sodium depletion impacts the taste of salt to drive sodium intake is unknown. Here we show that tongue gland-derived endothelin-1 (EDN1) regulates the amiloride-sensitive, sodium-selective salt taste. Edn1 is specifically expressed in the glands embedded within the tongue. Under normal conditions, EDN1 suppresses salt taste by acting on its receptor EDNRB on the projections of salt-sensing taste neurons innervating taste buds. When internal sodium levels drop, EDN1 expression decreases, lifting this inhibition and enhancing responses to salt. Applying EDN1 directly to the tongue, using a nonionic eutectic-based organogel (Neogel) delivery technology that we establish here, dampens the activity of the salt-sensing taste neurons and reduces salt intake and preference. Conversely, genetic deletion of Ednrb in taste neurons mimics the effects of sodium deficiency, enhancing salt-sensing neuron activity and increasing salt consumption. These findings reveal a peripheral mechanism that regulates salt taste and intake in response to internal sodium levels, highlighting a direct role of the taste pathway in maintaining nutrient homeostasis.

papers.title: Feedback reliability modulates learning-related dynamics of midfrontal error monitoring
papers.abstract: Learning from feedback requires the brain to evaluate both performance outcomes and the reliability of the information used for learning. This study examined the dynamics of neural performance monitoring during deterministic (100% reliable) and probabilistic (75% reliable) associative learning using two within-subject tasks with different stimulus materials. Behavioral performance improved under both feedback regimes, but learning was consistently more successful under deterministic feedback. Error-related negativity, feedback-related negativity, and phase-locked midfrontal theta became progressively more pronounced across deterministic learning, particularly in the image-image task, whereas corresponding changes were attenuated under probabilistic feedback. Induced theta showed the opposite pattern, decreasing across deterministic learning while remaining comparatively stable under probabilistic learning. These opposing theta trajectories suggest that phase-locked and induced activity reflect distinct components of learning-related neural adaptation that may be obscured when total theta power is considered alone. Overall, the findings indicate that feedback reliability shapes the progressive tuning of midfrontal performance-monitoring responses during learning.

papers.title: Sex differences in fear extinction are conditional, not categorical
papers.abstract: Threat memories are dynamic, and their behavioral expression can change with subsequent experience and the passage of time. Extinction training can reduce conditioned fear responses, yet these responses may re-emerge over time through spontaneous recovery. Although biological sex has been implicated as modulatory factor in fear and extinction memory processes, studies have reported inconsistent findings. Here, we investigated how differences in extinction training and the timing of memory assessment influence extinction memory in male and female mice. Using contextual fear conditioning, we assessed fear acquisition and threat retention, characterized within-session and across-session extinction during repeated training, and compared shorter (3-minute) and longer (6-minute) daily extinction sessions. We subsequently evaluated extinction memory retention and spontaneous recovery at a later time point. Estrous-cycle stage in females was monitored daily throughout the experimental protocol to examine its potential association with fear and extinction behavior. We found that males and females demonstrated comparable fear acquisition and threat memory, as well as similar extinction progression across days. During longer extinction sessions, but not shorter, males showed greater within-session reductions in freezing, whereas females exhibited modestly higher overall freezing. We found no significant sex difference in the magnitude of spontaneous recovery. There was no significant association between estrous-cycle stage and freezing behavior. Together, our findings suggest that sex-dependent differences in contextual fear extinction are not uniformly expressed, but rather depend on the experimental conditions under which extinction is assessed

papers.title: Natural predator-associated chemosignals evoke distinct spatiotemporal patterns of risk assessment and vomeronasal population responses
papers.abstract: Natural predator-associated chemosignals elicit diverse defensive behaviors, yet it remains unclear how complex natural cues shape the spatiotemporal organization of risk assessment and activate vomeronasal sensory neurons (VSNs) and downstream circuits in the mammalian accessory olfactory system. Here, we investigated odor-dependent behavioral organization and VSN sensory representations using three-dimensional behavioral tracking, integrative machine-learning analysis, volumetric calcium imaging, and whole-brain FosTRAP2 mapping. We developed a pose-based integrative machine-learning analysis pipeline (PIMAP) to identify behavioral signatures based on posture, spatial exploration, state transitions, and temporal dynamics. We found that common behavioral states were expressed in multiple odor conditions, but their expression rates, spatial positions, and temporal sequencing distinguished responses to snake, tortoise, lizard, and mouse fecal cues. Snake fecal cues elicited sustained direct investigation and distinct patterns of spatial exploration, behavioral transitions, and grooming in both two-chamber and multiple-choice assays. Volumetric calcium imaging in the vomeronasal epithelium revealed distinct patterns of VSN activation by different reptilian cues. Whole-brain microscopy of FosTRAP2 transgenic mice indicated potential differential activity patterns in AOS-associated circuits following snake and tortoise exposure. Furthermore, Trpc2 deletion altered snake-associated behavioral signatures, while odor-discriminative behavioral patterns remained detectable. Together, these findings show that reptilian predator cues activate distinct AOS components and bias exploration patterns towards threat assessment and vigilance.

papers.title: Assessing reinforcement learning and vigor with an online decision-making battery
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning and vigor are two fundamental aspects of decision-making modulated by dopamine. Although vigor is highly relevant for mood disorders, it has been overlooked by previous batteries characterizing decision-making abilities. We developed a test battery with two RL tasks (RL/working memory, go/no-go task) and two vigor tasks (physical effort discounting, foraging task) and administered it to an online community sample (N = 162). We used computational modeling and factor analysis to identify two factors reflecting RL and vigor. The RL factor reflected participants' general decision-making ability, while vigor corresponded to a motivational propensity to obtain rewards. Both factors demonstrated moderately strong test-retest reliability (ICC(2,1) = .65 and .67, respectively) over a one-to-two-week interval. Moreover, both factors were meaningfully related to self-report scales. The RL and vigor factors were negatively and positively associated with mania, respectively, although further analyses revealed that vigor was not fully independent of RL. Neither factor was significantly associated with depression symptoms. Collectively, we present preliminary evidence that vigor may represent a separate factor from RL in line with the putative dopamine hypothesis, paving the way for future longitudinal assessments of RL and vigor in mood disorders.

papers.title: In-vivo MRI of noradrenergic and dopaminergic nuclei predicts future cognition and Alzheimers disease progression
papers.abstract: Noradrenergic and dopaminergic nuclei modulate cognition, and post-mortem data indicate they are affected early in the neurodegenerative cascade of Alzheimers disease. We derived in-vivo locus coeruleus (LC) and substantia nigra-ventral tegmental area (SN-VTA) MRI integrity measures from 739 ADNI participants, examined MRI-histology correspondence in individuals with both in-vivo imaging and post-mortem data, and tested whether these measures reflect early MRI-indexed degeneration predicting later cognitive decline. LC and SN-VTA contrast predicted cognitive and behavioral function 10 years later, despite only weak associations with current function. LC- and SN-VTA-associated brain-wide atrophy patterns aligned with PET-derived norepinephrine-transporter and dopamine-receptor maps, respectively. A one-standard-deviation decrease in baseline LC contrast was associated with 84% higher five-year odds of MCI-to-AD progression, and predictive effects of the catecholaminergic nuclei were mediated by their corresponding atrophy patterns. The SN-VTA pattern was associated with less amyloid PET-related memory decline. Together, these findings establish LC and SN-VTA MRI contrast as markers of early neurodegeneration that forecast cognitive decline years before clinical onset.

papers.title: Resource competition controls the length-dependence of synaptic protein synthesis
papers.abstract: Synaptic plasticity is dependent on the availability of specific proteins at the synapse with distinct requirements for potentiation and depression. Specifically, experimental evidence suggests an upregulation of short proteins and a downregulation for long proteins during long-term depression (LTD). The mechanism of this length-dependent protein synthesis regulation is yet unknown. In this work, we propose an computational model of ribosomal regulation of protein synthesis than can reproduce the length-dependent shift in protein expression seen during ribosomal elevations. By analysing the model dynamics, we discover that this effect is due to a shift from initiation-restricted to elongation-restricted protein synthesis. This works offers a novel explanation for the loss of ribosomal control of protein synthesis due to saturation in pathological ribosome enriched conditions. This new theoretical model of ribosomal regulation of protein synthesis is capable of explaining length-dependent shifts in protein synthesis.

papers.title: Dissection of the contribution of bushy cell delays to sound localization in juvenile and adult Mongolian gerbils
papers.abstract: Sound sources along the azimuth generate interaural time differences in arrival (ITDs) at the ears. According to Jeffress hypothesis, ITDs are detected by coincidence-sensitive neurons of the medial superior olive (MSO) for which a differential axonal delay from each ear to the MSO compensates for the ITDs. The origin and development of these delays remain poorly understood. To this end, we made recordings from bushy cells (BCs), which project to both MSOs, in adult and in 2-4-week-old Mongolian gerbils of either sex. First spike latency revealed a frequency-dependent delay likely originating in the cochlea. Latencies were markedly larger for pure tone stimulation than for complex sounds. Combined with our published recordings from the MSO, we observed a developmental decrease in most delays, including the contralateral BC-to-MSO axonal delay. Unexpectedly, the ipsilateral BC-to-MSO axonal delay did not decrease. Anatomical brainstem reconstructions revealed that the inter-MSO distance was stable whereas the cochlear nucleus-to-MSO distance increased during development. Together, this indicated an increase in axonal propagation velocity, particularly for the contralateral projection. The variability in the averaged firing onset between BCs was found to be as large as the variance in bITDs, suggesting that BCs with matching firing onset are selected to converge onto the same MSO neuron. Together, our results indicate that the developmental speedup of ear-to-MSO delays contributes greatly to bringing the bITDs within their ecological range, but that the difference in path length is not overcome, keeping the ITD tuning biased to contralateral sound sources.

papers.title: Expertise modifies neural responses to causal inference during language comprehension
papers.abstract: Linguistic communication relies on shared common ground, yet different individuals in a community have specialized semantic knowledge. As a key example, physicians acquire rich knowledge about the causes of illness. An open question is whether such "causal expertise" influences the neural basis of language comprehension. Here we tested the hypothesis that when understanding everyday language like, "Holly used a grimy faucet during her overseas plane ride. Now she has the stomach flu," medical experts retrieve richer representations in semantic networks of the brain. Physicians (n=16) and age- and education-matched controls (n=16) undergoing fMRI read two-sentence vignettes that elicited implicit causal inferences about illness or object mechanics as well as control vignettes that did not elicit causal inferences. Vignettes were linguistically matched across conditions and were accessible to experts and non-experts alike. Across both groups, causal vignettes about illness engaged a temporoparietal semantic network previously implicated in thinking about animates, i.e., people and animals (precuneus and left temporoparietal junction), whereas causal vignettes about object mechanics engaged a semantic network associated with places and objects. Critically, physicians' responses in the animacy network were more robust and self-similar, suggesting the activation of richer semantic knowledge. Medical expertise effects were specific to biological inferences rather than mechanical or mental state inferences. By contrast, individually localized frontotemporal language and frontoparietal reasoning networks did not respond preferentially to causally connected sentences or show effects of expertise. Our findings suggest that causal expertise alters neural responses to causal inferences that unfold automatically during language comprehension.

papers.title: Neuronal and glial transcriptional states vary with proximity to tangle-bearing neurons in the human entorhinal cortex
papers.abstract: More neurons die in Alzheimer's disease than form tangles, and tangle-bearing neurons can persist for decades, so tangles alone cannot explain degeneration. We combined 6,000-plex spatial transcriptomics with PHF1 immunofluorescence (167,176 cells; 9 donors) and imaging mass cytometry (170,195 cells; 62 donors), measuring each cell's distance to the nearest tangle. Tangle-bearing layer 2-3 excitatory neurons were enriched late along a trajectory of increasing microtubule-associated, synaptic and V-ATPase expression, with elevated p62 and K48-ubiquitin. Tangle-free neurons shared more of this state the closer they lay to a tangle, including higher chaperone and autophagy scores, p62 and nuclear size. Nearby glia had higher disease-associated scores, with astrocytes expressing less GFAP. Excitatory, but not inhibitory, neuron loss was greatest in subtypes closest to tangles and cortical depths richest in phosphorylated tau. Selective neuronal vulnerability may reflect not only a neuron's susceptibility to forming a tangle but also where it lies relative to one.

papers.title: Molecular MRI of Neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's Disease using a Folate-targeted Nanoprobe
papers.abstract: Background: Neuroinflammation, driven by activated microglia, plays a central role in the pathogenesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Non-invasive imaging of neuroinflammation holds promise for advancing our understanding of disease mechanisms and evaluating anti-inflammatory therapeutic strategies. The folate receptor (FR), specifically its {beta} isoform, has been identified as a marker of pro-inflammatory myeloid cells in peripheral inflammatory diseases; however, its association with AD neuroinflammation remains unknown. In this work, we first determined FR expression in microglia in mouse models of AD and subsequently evaluated molecular MRI (mMRI) using a folate-targeted nanoprobe for in vivo imaging of the folate receptor expression. Methods and results: Microglial activation and FR expression in APP/PS1 and P301S transgenic mouse models of AD was measured using flow cytometry. A FR-targeted nanoprobe for mMRI was prepared by functionalizing high T1-relaxivity liposomal gadolinium nanoparticle with folic acid. Following intravenous injection, localization of the nanoprobe in the brains of aged transgenic and wild-type mice was measured using T1-weighted MRI. Post-mortem microscopy measured nanoprobe localization relative to microglia and amyloid pathology. In both mouse models, FR{beta} was significantly (p < 0.05) upregulated in pro-inflammatory microglia expressing TNF and IL-1{beta}. The folate-targeted nanoprobe demonstrated MR signal enhancement in the cortical and hippocampal regions of transgenic mice but not in wild type mice; non-targeted nanoprobe control did not demonstrate signal enhancement in brain of transgenic mice. Microscopy confirmed colocalization of FR-targeted nanoprobe with IBA1-positive microglia/macrophages and amyloid plaques. Conclusions: Pro-inflammatory microglia exhibit elevated levels of FR, and its measurement by non-invasive mMRI is a promising marker of neuroinflammation in AD.

papers.title: Infection-related images reduce cortical edge metastability: a specification-curve analysis of a block-design fMRI study
papers.abstract: Cues of infection evoke disgust, attentional capture, withdrawal and shifts in social orientation, a set of responses attributed to the behavioral immune system. Responses this varied have to be coordinated, as the effects of inflammation are, so they should be visible in whole-cortex coupling. We predicted that infection-related images hold cortical dynamics in a narrower repertoire, reducing cortical edge metastability, the temporal variability of mean cofluctuation across parcel pairs. In two fMRI runs, 44 adults viewed alternating 18-s blocks of infection-related and neutral images; the primary test was specified before we looked at the data. That test gave Cohen's d = -0.31 (permutation p = .042), and 263 of 480 specifications were significant, all negative (joint p < .001). With global signal regression, the synchrony-based reduction survived removal of the stimulus-locked response, detrending, and motion, white-matter and cerebrospinal-fluid regression (d = -0.47), recurred in the second run (d = -0.44), and was smaller on strictly alternating blocks (d = -0.36). Without global signal regression, the pre-specified effect did not survive white-matter and cerebrospinal-fluid regression. Individual-difference predictions were not supported, and participants' contrasts did not replicate across runs. Infection-related images reduce the variability of residual global cofluctuation at the group level; whether this is specific to pathogen cues remains open.

papers.title: The ViRA-L (Visual Recognition Assessment-Leuven): Development, Validation, and Age Stratified Normative Characterization of a Multi-Category Visual Recognition Battery
papers.abstract: Objective: To develop and validate the Visual Recognition Assessment-Leuven (ViRA-L), a recognition-memory battery assessing ten visual categories within a matched task structure, and provide age-stratified normative data. Method: Healthy Dutch-speaking adults completed a visual recognition task for ten categories. Each category included six targets, 18 Learning trials, and 30 Novel trials requiring recognition across appearance changes. After exclusions, 417 participants remained. We evaluated reliability, score distributions, task effects, demographic associations, and category-specific norms. Results: Battery-level internal consistency was good (Cronbach's = .879; omega total = .901), with lower category-level estimates, broad score dispersion, and minimal floor and ceiling effects. Novel and difficult trials produced lower accuracy and slower responses. Age was the clearest demographic correlate of accuracy; gender and education showed no independent overall associations. Age effects varied by category and were larger in Novel than Learning trials. Model-based differences between ages 50 and 85 were largest for Pseudowords and Hands and smallest for Houses. Conclusions: The ViRA-L supports comparison of recognition-memory profiles under matched procedures. Category-dependent age associations support age-sensitive, category-specific interpretation. The battery provides a foundation for neuropsychological research; further validation is required for clinical diagnostic use.

papers.title: Phenotypic screening in Parkinson's iPSC-dopamine neurons identifies the FASN-SREBP1 axis as a potential therapeutic target
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) remains highly challenging to model in vitro, particularly when seeking robust functional phenotypes for target discovery. Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell dopaminergic neurons (iPSC-DANs) offer a promising platform to address this challenge. Because calcium dyshomeostasis is well-described in PD pathophysiology, it offers a platform for phenotypic screening. We have previously shown that GBA-N370S iPSC-DANs display impaired intracellular calcium release. Here, we used this disease-relevant phenotype to undertake a 4,108-compound phenotypic screen in GBA-N370S (GBA-NS) iPSC-DANs. This screen identified fatty acid synthase (FASN) as the most enriched protein target. The ability of compounds to rescue calcium release correlated with biochemical potency against FASN across multiple chemical series. We confirmed that FASN knockdown increased intracellular calcium release, supporting an on-target effect. Untargeted lipidomics demonstrated broad remodelling of the neuronal lipidome after FASN inhibition, confirming target engagement. FASN inhibition also increased active a-glucocerebrosidase (GCase), reduced extracellular a-synuclein release and ER stress, and altered RASGRF1 expression. Mechanistically, FASN inhibition activated sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1 (SREBP1), and SREBP1 overexpression alone was sufficient to increase intracellular calcium release, identifying a FASN-SREBP1-calcium homeostasis axis in human neurons. Finally, the FASN inhibitor BI 99179 achieved brain exposure and reduced brain fatty acid levels while inducing an SRE-associated transcriptional response in a Parkinson's mouse model, providing evidence of in vivo target engagement. These findings establish patient iPSC-neuron functional screening as a tractable discovery platform to identify targets which can be taken in vivo and nominate the FASN-SREBP1 axis as a candidate therapeutic pathway in PD.

papers.title: Cortical long-range dynamics track excitation-inhibition balance across cognitive states and organizational principles
papers.abstract: A fundamental question in systems neuroscience is how the brain's excitation-inhibition (E/I) balance shapes the temporal structure of neural activity and whether we can non-invasively recover this relationship from neural scaling properties. We show that MRS-derived E/I balance is expressed in long-range temporal dynamics and constrained by cytoarchitecture. The laminar organisation of inhibitory circuits, spanning agranular to granular cortex, determines how faithfully regional dynamics reflect E/I balance. This neurochemical signature is state-dependent: its relationship with cortical dynamics reverses during task engagement, consistent with traversal of dynamical regimes around a critical point. It extends beyond fMRI to arousal-linked dynamics, indexed by pupil diameter and microsaccades, indicating a global mode of cortical state rather than a regionally isolated property. The imprint of E/I balance on long-range dynamics follows the sensory-association axis at rest, and is reconfigured during task engagement. These findings establish E/I balance as a neurochemical quantity with structured, scalable signatures across the temporal and spatial organization of the human cortex.

papers.title: A Unified World Model in Human Posterior Parietal Cortex
papers.abstract: How does the brain understand the physical world, predict future events, and plan actions? Are these problems solved by a unified world model, as hypothesized by cognitive scientists and artificial intelligence researchers? Posterior parietal cortex has been implicated in all these functions, but whether the same neurons support each of them is unknown. We recorded from the superior parietal lobule (SPL) of two tetraplegic participants implanted with microelectrode arrays. SPL units preferentially engaged by intuitive physics, judging block-tower stability and viewing naturalistic physical events, also predicted whether moving objects would collide hundreds of milliseconds before contact, generalizing between different physical scenarios. These populations also encoded which hand action the participant intended to perform. These findings identify SPL as a substrate for physical world modeling.

papers.title: Superior Frontal Gyrus Cortical Thickness Mediates the Association Between Openness to Experience and Theory of Mind: Evidence from the Human Connectome Project
papers.abstract: Background: Theory of mind (ToM), the capacity to infer the mental states of others, varies considerably across healthy adults. Openness to experience has been linked both to social-cognitive abilities and to thinner prefrontal cortex, but whether cortical structure statistically accounts for the association between openness and ToM is unknown. We tested whether bilateral superior frontal gyrus (SFG) cortical thickness mediates this association. Methods: Data from 1,049 healthy young adults with complete data were drawn from the Human Connectome Project. ToM was indexed by accuracy on the Heider-Simmel social animation task, openness by the NEO Five-Factor Inventory, and SFG thickness by FreeSurfer. Models adjusted for age, sex, intracranial volume and fluid intelligence; indirect effects were tested with 5,000 bootstrap resamples, and Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction was applied. Results: Openness showed a positive total effect on ToM accuracy (beta = .081, p = .009). Higher openness was associated with thinner left and right SFG (beta = -.085 and -.084), and thinner SFG with higher ToM accuracy (beta = -.082 and -.075). Indirect effects were significant (left: .0069, 95% CI [.0010, .0158]; right: .0063, 95% CI [.0007, .0146]), accounting for approximately 8.5% and 7.8% of the total effect, and remained significant after rank-based normalisation of the ceiling-affected ToM scores. Conclusions: SFG cortical thickness partially and statistically mediates the association between openness to experience and social cognition. Because the data are cross-sectional and effects are small, the findings do not establish a causal mechanism, neural efficiency or synaptic pruning, but they identify a candidate structural pathway for longitudinal testing.

papers.title: The human-specific gene FRMPD2B couples postnatal experience to the expansion of cortical connectivity
papers.abstract: The human neocortex is characterized by its uniquely prolonged postnatal developmental period during which experience sculpts neuronal circuits, a process essential to human cognitive abilities. Yet whether human-specific genetic innovations have shaped the activity-dependent mechanisms regulating circuit assembly remains unknown. Here, we identify the human-specific gene FRMPD2B as an activity- and experience-regulated modifier of cortical connectivity. FRMPD2B is primarily expressed in cortico-cortical projection neurons postnatally and throughout childhood. It promotes dendritic, axonal and synaptic development, and is required for proper morphogenesis in xenotransplanted human cortical neurons. FRMPD2B expression is bidirectionally regulated by neuronal activity and experience. This activity-responsiveness was gained after FRMPD2B arose through partial gene duplication, when a retrotransposon insertion remodeled its promoter. Our findings highlight how a series of genetic innovations have led to the emergence of a human-specific activity-regulated developmental program through which postnatal experience drives cortical connectivity expansion, linking genome evolution to human brain plasticity.

papers.title: Human iEEG recordings during audiovisual speech violations support and extend predictive routing models
papers.abstract: Rather than constantly reconstructing the world solely through sensory input, predictive processing theories posit that the brain utilizes predictions maintained as internal representations to guide sensory processing. An emerging model, predictive routing, proposes that an interplay between neuronal gamma (40-150 Hz) and alpha-beta (10-30 Hz) rhythms implements a dynamic mechanism for predictive processing. Namely, predictions enhance alpha-beta oscillations that suppress gamma activity during the processing of predicted inputs. While this model is supported by animal studies, its validity has not been fully explored within the human brain. The present study addresses this by leveraging human intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings across superior temporal and prefrontal/premotor areas of seven presurgical epilepsy patients during an audiovisual speech paradigm. We calculated iEEG power in the theta, alpha-beta, and high gamma bands during simple auditory deviance, multisensory integration, and a condition where an incongruent visual cue (lip movements) clashed with an auditory stimulus (a syllable), creating audiovisual incongruence that can elicit the McGurk illusion. Results revealed increased high-gamma and decreased alpha-beta power in the superior temporal cortex in response to auditory deviance and the McGurk condition, while frontal areas, despite reflecting a similar decrease in alpha-beta power, did not present this high gamma prediction error signal. Instead, the theta band revealed a strong prediction error signal in the McGurk condition, consistent with theories on the role of theta in reorganizing cortical networks. These results both support and extend existing predictive routing models for human-specific forms of predictive processing.

papers.title: Recurrent Spiking Neural Networks for Continuous Motor Control: A Biologically Plausible Model of Motor Cortex
papers.abstract: Motor cortex acquires skilled movements through recurrent spiking dynamics and experience-dependent synaptic plasticity, yet how such circuits learn continuous motor control using biologically local signals remains unclear. Here, we develop a recurrent spiking neural network model of motor cortex that addresses both the computational and biological requirements of motor learning. We first analytically derived the recurrent firing-rate state directly from synaptic input and trained the network by implicit differentiation, thereby avoiding backpropagation through long spike trajectories. We then introduced State-Carry Initialization, which enables closed-loop motor control by continuously carrying the ongoing recurrent state across successive actions. Building on this formulation, we devised a learning rule termed Feedback-Spike Nudging (FSN), in which teaching signals are delivered as spikes through a feedback pathway. Synaptic changes depend only on presynaptic activity and the feedback-evoked change in postsynaptic firing, consistent with biological mechanisms of synaptic plasticity in motor cortex. The resulting networks learned continuous motor control through both supervised and reinforcement learning, which could be mapped respectively onto interactions of motor cortex with the cerebellum and basal ganglia. Moreover, the FSN learning rule was consistent with experimental observations of structural spine plasticity in mouse motor cortex. Thus, our study lays a foundation for recurrent spiking models of motor cortex that are biologically grounded at both the functional and anatomical levels.

papers.title: The Canadian Pediatric Imaging Platform (C-PIP) Reference Sample: Neuroimaging Protocol and Cross-site Validation for Harmonized Multimodal Pediatric Imaging
papers.abstract: Understanding how the human brain matures from infancy through adolescence is essential for identifying factors that influence health outcomes. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides powerful tools for characterizing structural, microstructural, functional, and metabolic aspects of brain development; however, many pediatric imaging studies are constrained by small sample sizes, limited geographic diversity, lack of longitudinal measurement, restricted age ranges, and heterogeneous acquisition protocols. While recent large-scale neuroimaging consortia have begun to address these challenges, such resources remain limited in the Canadian context, creating a critical gap. The Canadian Pediatric Imaging Platform (C-PIP) has developed a multisite neuroimaging framework across three of Canada's largest pediatric hospitals: Alberta Children's Hospital (Calgary), Centre Hospitalier Universitaire Sainte-Justine (Montreal), and the Hospital for Sick Children (Toronto). These three sites were united through a national initiative, leveraging high-performance MRI systems to accelerate Canadian neurodevelopmental research. In addition, C-PIP has implemented a centralized data sharing infrastructure to facilitate open science and collaborative research across institutions. Here, we describe the development and implementation of a multimodal MRI acquisition protocol designed to support multimodal longitudinal studies of typical and atypical brain development spanning infancy through adolescence. Within-site stability and cross-site stability of C-PIP core MRI sequences were evaluated using a travelling-participant study. The C-PIP MRI protocol establishes a harmonized, multisite imaging framework that supports large-scale investigations of pediatric brain development and disorders.

papers.title: Automated multiscale high-content imaging connects plaque population heterogeneity to localized synapse loss
papers.abstract: Synapse loss is a major correlate of cognitive decline in neurodegenerative disease, yet its relationship to localized pathology remains difficult to study at scale. Conventional confocal imaging approaches are limited by low throughput, selection bias, and restricted sampling of pathological features. Here, we describe an automated high-content imaging and analysis workflow that enables large-scale quantification of amyloid beta plaque-associated synapse loss within mouse brain tissue. Using Preciscan-based multiscale acquisition on the Opera Phenix platform, this workflow combines tissue-wide pathology mapping with targeted high-magnification imaging and subcellular analysis. We apply this framework to acquire and analyze hundreds of plaque images in the CRND8 mouse model of A{beta} proteinopathy, demonstrating plaque-associated synapse loss within developing plaque populations over disease progression. We find that small diffuse plaques accumulate rapidly at late stages in CRND8, but that the primary synapse loss comes from large cored plaques. More broadly, this scalable framework enables systematic investigation of subcellular phenomena across pathological microenvironments in disease models.

papers.title: Structural Evolution of Neural Networks during Zebrafish Early Development
papers.abstract: The spatial architecture of neural networks underpins nervous system function, yet dynamic in vivo evidence for their early establishment process remains scarce. Here, using long-term confocal live-cell imaging of transgenic zebrafish, we dissected neural network development across the brain, yolk sac, and spinal cord at single-cell resolution. We reveal that repeated growth cone bifurcation is the fundamental cellular mechanism for network node formation. Despite distinct developmental origins, networks in all three regions exhibit highly conserved dynamics, strictly following Strahler hierarchical ordering and Hack's power-law scaling. Quantitative topological analysis shows that as development progresses, node numbers and clustering coefficients increase, while network density decreases. This reflects a structural optimization strategy balancing high functional efficiency with low wiring cost. These findings suggest that physical and geometric constraints, combined with simple local rules, drive the self-organization of complex neural networks, offering valuable principles for artificial network design.

papers.title: Beyond rumination: an ecological momentary assessment of daily thinking patterns in maladaptive daydreaming
papers.abstract: Maladaptive daydreaming is a form of maladaptive repetitive thought characterized by excessive, dysfunctional fantasy engagement, with notable links to psychological distress and poor well-being. Although symptoms can be reliably measured along a continuum, it remains unclear how they manifest in the phenomenological characteristics of everyday thinking, as well as which thought characteristics are unique to maladaptive daydreaming versus shared with trait rumination, a transdiagnostic manifestation of maladaptive repetitive thinking that frequently co-occurs with maladaptive daydreaming. To advance these questions, we conducted a pre-registered study using ecological momentary assessment to track the everyday thoughts of 446 young adults (aged 18 to 34) spanning a range of maladaptive daydreaming symptom severity as assessed with the 16-item Maladaptive Daydreaming Scale. Higher maladaptive daydreaming scores were associated with several poor mental health indicators, including higher trait rumination. Positive associations between maladaptive daydreaming scores and both negatively-valenced and task-unrelated thinking emerged, yet these relationships were accounted for by variance shared with rumination. Beyond rumination, higher maladaptive daydreaming scores were uniquely associated with worse mood, as well as greater internally-oriented attention, more socially-oriented thought, and greater overall thought persistence. Maladaptive daydreaming also uniquely moderated the relationship between internal orientation and social orientation, such that the positive association between internal and social thought content became stronger at higher levels of maladaptive daydreaming. Overall, these findings provide novel evidence that maladaptive daydreaming levels are linked to unique socioemotional features and restricted dynamics, beyond its overlap with general ruminative distress in everyday life. These insights suggest that clinical interventions should target immersive fantasy engagement alongside transdiagnostic maladaptive repetitive thinking.

papers.title: An atlas of the aging glycoproteome reveals how glycosylation modulates autoantibody binding in the brain
papers.abstract: N-glycosylation generates substantial molecular diversity, yet how glycan composition varies throughout aging remains poorly understood. We mapped the N-glycoproteome of brain, liver, spleen, kidney, and plasma across nine ages spanning the mouse lifespan, identifying 80,618 unique N-glycopeptides at 9,211 glycosites on 4,391 glycoproteins, together with matched proteomic trajectories (glycoproteinatlas.org). Organ identity was the dominant determinant of glycan composition, but numerous glycosites nevertheless underwent remodeling with age. The brain showed a prominent age-associated increase in short paucimannose glycans, driven in part by the age-associated increase in the glycan-processing enzyme HEXB. In white matter, a hotspot for this change, aging increased the paucimannosylation of Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG), a major target of central nervous system autoimmunity. We identified MOG-reactive autoantibodies in aged individuals and patients with MOG antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) and showed that the glycan at MOG N60 modulates autoantibody binding. Experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) recapitulated a subset of the age-associated glycosite changes, revealing shared glycosylation signatures between aging and autoimmune targeting of MOG. Together, these findings reveal site-specific N-glycosylation as both a marker of age and a regulator of molecular interactions.

papers.title: HERC1 Loss of Function Causes a Developmental Disorder with Impaired Hippocampal Function
papers.abstract: Pathogenic variants in HERC1 are associated with a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by macrocephaly, developmental delay, intellectual disability, and psychomotor dysfunction. Although genetic and molecular studies suggest a loss-of-function mechanism, definitive in vivo evidence that HERC1 deficiency is sufficient to cause neurodevelopmental abnormalities is lacking. Using a HERC1 knockout mouse model, we investigated the behavioural, neuronal, and synaptic consequences of complete HERC1 loss. HERC1 deficiency caused motor coordination and cognitive deficits in both sexes, while male mutants additionally displayed hyperactivity and increased anxiety-like behaviour. Histological analyses revealed selective hippocampal abnormalities, including disruption of dentate gyrus organization, whereas Purkinje cells survival and cerebellar compartmentalization remained preserved. HERC1-deficient mice exhibited a marked increase in hippocampal GABAergic interneurons, impaired maturation of dendritic spines in CA1 pyramidal neurons, and altered adult neurogenesis, indicating widespread defects in hippocampal circuit organization. Consistent with these structural abnormalities, glutamatergic synaptic components were significantly altered throughout the hippocampus. These molecular changes showed a sex-dependent pattern, with predominantly presynaptic defects in males and postsynaptic alterations in females. Despite these differences, whole-cell recordings revealed a common functional phenotype in both sexes. At both mossy fibre-CA3 and Schaffer collateral-CA1 synapses, HERC1-deficient neurons exhibited a progressive inability to sustain excitatory neurotransmission during repetitive stimulation, resulting in impaired steady-state glutamatergic transmission. Together, these findings demonstrate that loss of HERC1 function is sufficient to produce a neurodevelopmental phenotype and identify HERC1 as a critical regulator of hippocampal circuit assembly and function. Our results provide mechanistic insight into the pathogenesis of HERC1-associated disorders and establish the Herc1 knockout mouse as a preclinically relevant model for investigating disease mechanisms and therapeutic approaches.

papers.title: State-dependent modulation of cross-area sensory processing in mouse neocortex
papers.abstract: Perception and decision-making rely on distributed cortical circuits that transform sensory inputs into choices and actions. Such cortical processing varies with behavioral state, such that the same inputs can be handled differently across states. However, how behavioral state shapes sensory processing across distributed brain regions remains unclear. To address this question, we trained mice to perform a two-alternative choice task that required discrimination between paired auditory and whisker cues. During task training, we simultaneously recorded neuronal population activity from the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and the posterior parietal cortex (PPC), using two-photon imaging of neurons expressing the fluorescent calcium indicator GCaMP6f. Using a Hidden Markov Model with Generalized Linear Models (GLM-HMM), we identified three latent behavioral states, including one optimal-performing stimulus-guided state and two sub-optimal biased states. We found that the optimal state was associated with stronger sensory representation in S1 and PPC, as well as stronger bottom-up information transfer from S1 to anterior PPC (PPC-A). In contrast, biased states showed weaker sensory coding and relatively stronger involvement of rostrolateral PPC (PPC-RL). State-dependent differences were present in both task-related and task-orthogonal population activity. These results show that internal states modulate not only local sensory encoding, but also the routing of task-relevant information across cortical networks.
